subject.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands

question: How should Lobster represent cancellation that arrives during a side-effecting command after that command completes successfully but before later pipeline stages start?
rationale: The runtime must preserve the definitive result of the completed email send while also preventing downstream execution; current contracts do not clearly designate whether an ordinary halt result or a distinct cancelled-partial-output outcome is intended.

options.title: Halt with completed output
options.body: Return the completed send results with a pipeline halt so later stages do not start, documenting this as the supported partial-cancellation contract.

options.title: Add cancelled partial output
options.body: Introduce an explicit runtime outcome that carries completed results while marking the overall workflow cancelled and suppressing later stages.

options.title: Fail after send settlement
options.body: Throw after the in-flight send settles, preventing downstream work but omitting its completed result from the normal output.

recommendation.title: Halt with completed output
recommendation.body: Return the completed send results with a pipeline halt so later stages do not start, documenting this as the supported partial-cancellation contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent tool-runtime work makes them the strongest available owner for the output-envelope and pipeline-halt contract.
